en.title: US Senators Seek Extension of Transit Accessibility Funding Program
en.summary: US senators are advocating to extend the All Stations Accessibility Program, which funds upgrades to make transit stations fully accessible for people with disabilities. Meanwhile, Illinois is deploying Meta smart glasses and AI-powered glasses to assist users with disabilities, while advocates call for greater understanding of disabilities in Japan. Additionally, new guidance outlines how organizations can conduct accessibility audits to comply with the European Accessibility Act.

highlights.title: U.S. Senators push to extend the All Stations Accessibility Program
Illinois Assistive Technology Program uses Meta glasses to improve accessibility
AI smart glasses connect perception, memory, and accessibility to support low-vision users - Designboom
Call for Greater Understanding of Disabilities in Japan
Accessibility Audit: How to Ensure EAA Compliance

zh-TW.title: 美國參議員推動延長所有車站無障礙計畫
zh-TW.summary: 美國參議員倡議延長所有車站無障礙計畫，以資助交通車站的無障礙改造，使其對殘障人士完全可用。同時，伊利諾伊州正部署Meta智慧眼鏡與AI眼鏡，協助殘障使用者；慕尼黑機場成為德國首家獲得ACI無障礙認證的機場。此外，日本的殘障理解呼籲在社群媒體上引起關注，強調需要提升大眾對殘障的認識。

highlights.title: 美國參議員推動延長所有車站無障礙計畫
